bull.b: Danaher’s installed-base model produces cash beyond accounting earnings, funding R&D, acquisitions and shareholder returns while reducing dependence on periodic instrument sales. High conversion indicates durable economics across research, diagnostics and bioprocessing workflows.

Recurring reagents, consumables, software and service revenue tied to mission-critical instruments can deepen customer retention and create lifecycle revenue. Once platforms are adopted in regulated workflows, switching costs and repeat usage support demand resilience.

bull.t: Improving Core Growth and Portfolio Expansion
bull.b: Underlying demand is improving while portfolio additions broaden growth exposure: core ex-respiratory growth accelerated, EPS guidance rose, and Masimo plus StatLab add diagnostics scale and recurring revenue. This supports medium-term portfolio expansion.

bear.t: Modest Revenue Growth and Lower Returns
bear.b: TTM revenue growth is only ~1.3% after softer 2023–2025 performance, while net margin and ROE remain below 2021–2022 peaks. This suggests recovery is gradual and leaves earnings more reliant on productivity and portfolio execution.

Delayed chromatography resin shipments and limited visibility into customer production schedules can create multi-quarter revenue volatility. Even with healthy orders, site-readiness and shipment timing may defer bioprocessing growth and reduce planning confidence.

Softness in North America and Western Europe, alongside under-normal academic funding, can delay instrument purchases and research spending. Although academia is less than 5% of revenue, prolonged weakness may constrain recovery in research-oriented end markets.
